policy.equations: Named equation/model entries, not scalar component equations or mathematically disjoint families. Includes frameworks and auxiliary formulations; variants share one entry except the three separately explained SR/GR fluid systems. Biological entries are imported once from their own catalog.
policy.methods: Named numerical methods and building blocks with a reading chapter. Aliases count once; RK stages, dimensions, parameter combinations, mesh layouts and theoretical conditions do not add methods. A family and a separately explained algorithm may both appear. Not a count of mutually exclusive end-to-end solvers.
policy.papers: Unique bibliographic publications classified as journal articles or conference papers, deduplicated by DOI or author/title/year. Includes reviews, translations and explicitly labeled accepted papers; not a claim that every full text was inspected. Books, chapters, reports, preprints and documentation are separate.
policy.references: Unique cataloged works across all publication types. An original publication and a later translation are separate works; duplicate DOI records are not. NASA case links in prose are not catalog records.
policy.test_problems: Count independent problems across published atlas results and the verified public code edition. Distinguish governing equations, dimensions, boundary conditions and named initial/source problems; merge solver, mesh, step-size, parameter-sweep, random-seed and presentation variants of the same problem. Repeated Sod exhibits, wedge Mach variants and CT/GLM variants do not add problems. Exclude reference-only evaluations, planned/literature-only entries, diagrams, and local identity/invariant/input-error unit checks. Static-force, boundary-value, approximation and algebraic problems are included; not every entry is a time-evolving simulation.

items.label: Lagrange nodal basis / GLL collocation
items.scope: Interval cardinal functions, modal transforms, exact versus quadrature mass, and P1/P2 triangle shapes.

items.label: Limited PPM reconstruction
items.scope: Method-of-lines parabolic FV and a separate direct-Eulerian traced primitive PPM with contact steepening and shock flattening switches. No Lagrange/remap or multidimensional CTU.

items.label: Euler characteristic reconstruction
items.scope: Local conservative FV basis or face-frozen Roe FD basis; controlled component/characteristic comparisons.

items.label: FD WENO5-Z
items.scope: Global LF splitting, exponent 2, fixed epsilon 1e-6; point values, not FV state interpolation.

items.label: AUSM-family flux splitting
items.scope: Arithmetic-sound-speed AUSM plus specified critical-sound-speed AUSM+ and AUSM+-up. Matched traced-PPM cases, a recorded strong-jump failure and forebody tests; no low-Mach PDE certification.

items.label: Logistic population growth
items.scope: One dimensionless population. Compare RK4 with the analytic solution at every output time; check nonnegativity and time refinement. Excludes reaction–diffusion and multispecies models.

items.label: Michaelis–Menten and full enzyme kinetics
items.scope: The 1913 rapid-equilibrium interpretation and the 1925 quasi-steady-state derivation must remain distinct.

items.label: McKendrick age-structured population
items.scope: This is the classical age-transport form; the later von Foerster lineage is acknowledged without treating its date as the first appearance.

items.label: SIR and SEIR compartment models
items.scope: Closed homogeneous population-fraction SIR. Compare RK4 with independently implemented SciPy DOP853; check conservation, nonnegativity and time convergence. Excludes SEIR, spatial spread and calibration to observations.

items.label: Fisher–KPP invasion front
items.scope: Fisher–KPP is a conventional family name; the independent KPP 1937 original remains an archival follow-up. The exact special speed is not the minimal speed.

items.label: Monod growth and chemostat
items.scope: This writes one constant-yield extension of saturation growth, not a universal metabolic model.

items.label: Hodgkin–Huxley membrane dynamics
items.scope: The original squid-axon model is not a calibrated human cardiac model. No single rate parameter set is selected by this survey.

items.label: Turing reaction–diffusion framework
items.scope: A 1D periodic Schnakenberg system of length 2pi, a=0.1, b=0.9 and diffusivities 0.01/1. Preserve the earlier linear-onset example and compare finite-amplitude nonlinear evolution and post-growth patterns from fixed reflection-symmetric data with independent Fourier–Galerkin/Radau references and separate spatial/temporal refinement. No general pattern selection, 2D, biological calibration or fluid-coupling claim.

items.label: FitzHugh–Nagumo excitation and recovery
items.scope: Scoped verification of an FHN/BVP-style reduced ODE. It excludes full HH ion channels, spatial axons, patient data and experimental electrophysiology reproduction.

items.label: Keller–Segel chemotaxis
items.scope: This is a common two-field reduction of a more detailed original formulation. Blowup thresholds depend on dimension, domain, boundary and chemical dynamics.

items.label: Gierer–Meinhardt activator–inhibitor
items.scope: Source densities, saturation and baseline production vary across the model family. This simplified formula is not a verbatim transcription of every original variant.

items.label: Fluid–elastic structure and immersed boundaries
items.scope: Immersed boundary is a numerical coupling method, not itself a closed biological constitutive equation. The existing periodic MAC solver does not implement this coupling.

items.label: Chemical master equation and Gillespie SSA
items.scope: The 1977 paper is a foundational SSA reference, not a priority claim for all master equations. SSA is a solver; the reaction network is the model. A seed documents a trajectory, not an ensemble validation.

items.label: Mackey–Glass delayed physiological feedback
items.scope: A scalar initial value alone is insufficient. The delayed ODE is distinct from a spatial reaction–diffusion model.

items.label: Replicator evolutionary game dynamics
items.scope: No universal Lyapunov function or equivalence of fixed point and evolutionarily stable strategy is assumed.

items.label: Schnakenberg reaction–diffusion
items.scope: A 1D periodic Schnakenberg system of length 2pi, a=0.1, b=0.9 and diffusivities 0.01/1. No general pattern selection, 2D, biological calibration or fluid-coupling claim.

items.label: Shigesada–Kawasaki–Teramoto cross-diffusion
items.scope: The displayed homogeneous-environment reduction omits the original environmental-potential terms. It is not equivalent to two independent scalar diffusion equations.

items.label: Gray–Scott spatial autocatalysis
items.scope: 1983 is the well-mixed CSTR source; Pearson 1993 is the spatial pattern reference. Spot division does not by itself demonstrate cell division or a linear Turing instability.

items.label: Aliev–Panfilov cardiac excitation
items.scope: Monodomain/bidomain tissue models add conductivity tensors and, for bidomain, an extracellular elliptic constraint. They are not automatically included by this two-variable model.

items.label: Repressilator mRNA–protein network
items.scope: The six-variable form is distinct from a reduced three-protein oscillator; oscillations are parameter-dependent.

items.label: Genetic toggle switch
items.scope: Bistability is not guaranteed for arbitrary Hill exponents or production rates. Induction, mRNA dynamics and noise are additional model choices.

items.label: Schrodinger eigenproblems
items.scope: Uniform radial-grid tests of isolated hydrogenic 1s, 2s, 2p and 3d states; not a direct general many-electron Schrödinger solver.

items.label: Stationary electronic Schrödinger equation
items.scope: Fixed-nuclei nonrelativistic electronic many-body eigenproblem; add nuclear repulsion separately. Runnable examples cover only isolated one-electron hydrogenic atoms, not direct general many-electron solutions.

items.label: Closed-shell Hartree–Fock equations
items.scope: Closed-shell RHF spatial-orbital equations, generally with nonlocal exchange. Runnable code is restricted to the spherical 1s² helium local reduction; general molecular/many-electron Fock-matrix construction is not implemented.

items.label: Local Kohn–Sham DFT
items.scope: Representative local KS equations. Runnable code covers spherical-helium spin-unpolarized Dirac exchange-only LDA. Correlation, GGA, hybrids, generalized KS and periodic systems are not implemented.

items.label: Time-dependent Kohn–Sham equations
items.scope: Representative local time-dependent KS equations. Distinguish initial-state dependence, exchange-correlation memory and adiabatic approximations. No dedicated real-time or response implementation is published.

items.label: Two-dimensional rotational advection
items.scope: Prescribed divergence-free solid rotation only; not Euler fluid dynamics or arbitrary velocity fields.

items.label: Level-set interface advection
items.scope: Prescribed2D rigid motions with analytic exterior data only. Normal-speed, curvature-driven and two-phase fluid equations are reading only.

items.label: Monte Carlo integration
items.scope: Integrate x² under U[0,1]. Compare 256 independent seeds with analytic integral and variance, checking N^-1/2 RMS scaling and interval coverage. Excludes MCMC and rare events.

items.label: Stochastic differential equations
items.scope: Euler–Maruyama for scalar geometric Brownian motion. Coarse/fine steps and analytic endpoints share the same Brownian paths; measure strong RMS error across 4096 paths. Does not validate general SDEs, MCMC or weak convergence order.

items.label: Automatic differentiation
items.scope: Limited to educational real forward mode and small dense-Newton Bratu comparisons. Reverse mode, HVPs and matrix-free Newton–Krylov remain explanatory only. A separate dedicated supplement verifies implicit sensitivities and discrete adjoints.

items.label: Implicit differentiation and adjoint methods
items.scope: The sensitivity edition verifies smooth lower-branch Bratu and a small nonsymmetric linear example with explicit adjoint pairing and objective quadrature. Separate inverse editions fit constant lambda and two spatial coefficients with regularization and identifiability checks. Time-dependent adjoints and shock sensitivities remain unimplemented.

items.label: Gradient and quasi-Newton optimization
items.scope: Educational tests use small smooth lower-branch Bratu problems and fixed synthetic observations. They cover two spatial coefficients, Tikhonov regularization, local data-sensitivity SVD, rank loss with central observations and reflection ambiguity. Prior selection through regularization does not add observational information. Real data, high-dimensional function estimation, global uniqueness, statistical confidence intervals and quasi-Newton methods generally are outside scope.

items.label: Yee finite-difference time-domain method
items.scope: Educational Yee FDTD: retained vacuum/Fresnel/s-p/PML examples plus r6 1D normal-incidence Ohmic and passive Lorentz slabs. Spectral references, R/T, direct dissipation, material storage, modified/physical budgets and space/time refinement are separate checks. Not blanket validation of general dispersion, multiple resonances, oblique dispersive incidence, dispersive PML or general 2D/3D.

items.label: Centered spatial difference
items.scope: Reaction-diffusion: separate second-order space and fourth-order time: Validate a small linear diffusion-reaction operator against continuous and semidiscrete Fourier solutions. Turing instability: linear growth and small-amplitude patterns: Use a matrix exponential to validate stable homogeneous kinetics and diffusion-driven growth of a selected Schnakenberg mode. Finite-amplitude Schnakenberg transient: nonlinearity and independent reference: Validate a finite-amplitude reaction-diffusion transient to t=8 with an independent Fourier–Galerkin reference, grid/time convergence and newly generated harmonics. Near-saturated Schnakenberg pattern: near-stationarity and grid/time convergence: Compare the selected1D pattern at t=100 with an independent reference. Separate reference90→100 change/full-PDE residual from the finite-step primary FD residual.

items.label: Upwind finite differences
items.scope: The additional Zalesak-type example is two-dimensional scalar rotation in a prescribed divergence-free velocity. Compare donor-cell upwinding and minmod MUSCL with the same periodic grid and SSPRK(3,3), measuring stage bounds, conservation and full-turn shape errors. It does not certify FCT or general multidimensional Euler bounds.

items.label: Lax–Friedrichs
items.scope: The additional double rarefaction connects one-dimensional conservative MUSCL, shared Lax–Friedrichs fluxes, mean-preserving positive-state scaling and SSPRK(3,3). Check the admissible CFL/wave-speed conditions, means and faces at each forward-Euler candidate/SSP stage, and conservation budgets; this does not certify general Euler, WENO, DG or MHD positivity.

items.label: MUSCL reconstruction
items.scope: Compare shock–density-wave interaction against separately executed Athena++ reference data rather than a finer grid of the same Python code. The additional Noh edition uses volume-centroid conservative MUSCL/minmod with Heun only in spherical runs; planar/cylindrical states stay piecewise constant. The additional low-Mach vortex uses the same unlimited central primitive reconstruction for both Roe variants. It does not verify general limited MUSCL or a TVD guarantee. items.label: Rusanov / local Lax–Friedrichs flux
items.scope: An original small 1D finite-volume code solves zero-pressure Noh flow in planar, cylindrical and spherical symmetry. Grids 64/128/256/512 measure full-domain error, origin heating, shock location and budgets, and compare spherical boundary-inflow time-quadrature error with its analytic identity. The additional2D Cartesian Noh edition updates both x/y fluxes and both momenta on a full square. The additional spherical Sedov blast measures grid and finite deposition-radius effects separately.

items.label: HLL
items.scope: Three-grid 2D Double Mach verification using HLL and Heun compares a separately written finite-grid numerical reference, boundary-flux budgets, shock position and unresolved near-wall structure. The additional forward-step example verifies actual 2D finite-volume flow with reflecting walls including the step faces. The additional Guderley example evolves a zero-upstream-pressure spherical converging shock only before collapse and compares a semi-analytic similarity reference.

items.label: Roe
items.scope: A fixed smooth 2D Euler isentropic vortex at background Mach numbers .1 and .01 compares ordinary Roe and Miczek-type dissipation-matrix preconditioning D=P⁻¹|PA|, with unlimited central primitive-variable MUSCL reconstruction for both. SSPRK(3,3) retains physical time and the acoustic CFL. Velocity error, dynamically normalized pressure error, periodic conservation and sampled Fourier diagnostics are evaluated separately. Pseudo-time or dual-time steady acceleration, slope limiting and TVD guarantees remain outside this example.

items.label: Constrained transport / CT
items.scope: Orszag–Tang: CT, GLM and independent Athena++: Compare CT and GLM density, magnetic field, conservation and div B for the same periodic Orszag–Tang data, against separately executed Athena++. CT and GLM: mesh/time convergence of a moving magnetostatic equilibrium: Use a constructed exact equilibrium with nonzero magnetic force balanced by a pressure gradient, matching CT/GLM initial cell states, flux speed bound and time-step sequence. Orszag–Tang: matched CT/GLM and converged independent references: Run CT/GLM with the same OT initial cell averages and dt sequence, comparing with separately executed Athena++ references whose mesh/time sensitivities are separated. Initial-constraint preservation by CT and active GLM cleaning: nonphysical control: Intentionally begin with the same non-solenoidal cell B, checking that CT does not remove the initial defect and calibrating GLM’s B/psi response. This diagnostic adds no physical problem.

items.label: Fast multipole translations
items.scope: 2D logarithmic FMM with M2M, M2L and L2L: Evaluate a free-space log potential with uniform-quadtree multipole and local expansions and compare with direct sums. FMM: direct and analytic references, order and tree depth: Compare a 96-particle 2D logarithmic kernel with independent all-pairs sums; measure order/depth, rotation/translation and approximate net-force errors.

items.label: HLLD MHD Riemann solver
items.scope: Compare the published HLLD-MC finite-volume code with Brio–Wu reference data independently produced by Athena++ at a pinned commit.

items.label: Ewald summation
items.scope: Neutral-cell Ewald sums and an independent theta integral: Implement real-space, reciprocal-space and self Ewald terms for neutral 3D periodic Coulomb charges; vary splitting and cutoffs. Ewald: asymmetric-cell energies and forces versus independent theta integration: Compare a neutral eight-charge cell energy and all 24 force components with a separately coded Gaussian/theta integral. Separate splitting and real/reciprocal truncation from invariants and conservation.

items.label: Particle mesh Ewald / PME
items.scope: Mesh/order convergence of B-spline smooth PME: A small smooth-PME example assigns charge with B-splines and evaluates the Ewald reciprocal contribution by FFT. SPME: mesh, interpolation order, mesh phase and conservation: Compare B-spline SPME with the same independent theta reference; measure mesh/order/phase effects, charge partition, energy gradients and net force.

items.label: Particle-in-cell / PIC
items.scope: Cold-plasma oscillation with electrostatic CIC PIC: Couple electrons to a 1D periodic grid by CIC, solving Poisson and particle motion self-consistently. PIC: mesh/time convergence, invariants and particle noise: Separate quiet-start refinement of a cold 1D periodic plasma from independent-seed initial particle noise; record charge, momentum, Gauss diagnostics and energy error.

items.label: Algebraic multigrid / AMG
items.scope: Matrix-based AMG: distinguish residual and solution error: Build a smoothed-aggregation hierarchy from an SPD matrix alone and run V-cycles. Problems with 7², 15² and 31² unknowns distinguish independent sparse direct solutions, analytic discrete sine modes and second-order convergence to the continuum solution. AMG: conditioning, anisotropy, residual and forward error: Separate condition number from anisotropy on SPD systems of 49, 225 and 961 unknowns. Compare analytic spectra, independent sparse direct solutions and DST diagonalization, and measure how residual translates to forward error.

items.label: QR, SVD and least squares
items.scope: Householder QR and one-sided Jacobi SVD: orthogonality, rank and least squares: Original Householder QR and one-sided Jacobi SVD for real tall matrices are checked on ordinary, 10⁶-column-scaled and rank-deficient inputs, against separate LAPACK singular values and minimum-norm least-squares solutions. QR/SVD: prescribed spectra, perturbation gain and numerical rank: Vary condition number from 1 to 2³⁶ for exactly representable 16×4 dyadic matrices, separating reconstruction from forward solution error. Compare LAPACK and separately executed 80/120-digit references for the actual binary64 inputs.

items.label: Krylov eigenvalue solvers
items.scope: Lanczos and Arnoldi: convergence of Ritz values and eigenpair residuals: Original Lanczos and Arnoldi on symmetric/nonsymmetric 32×32 and 48×48 matrices measure convergence of the largest-real-part eigenpair over Krylov dimensions 4, 8 and 16, against independent full-matrix LAPACK references. Krylov eigenvalues: cluster subspaces and nonnormal sensitivity: Measure Lanczos and Arnoldi with dimensions4/8/16/32 on 48-dimensional clustered symmetric and strongly nonnormal triangular matrices. Distinguish residual, forward error, eigenvalue condition number and invariant subspace.

items.label: Gaussian and adaptive quadrature
items.scope: Gauss–Legendre and adaptive quadrature: exactness, error estimates and budgets: Construct Gaussian nodes/weights from the Legendre recurrence and test polynomial moments through degree 2n−1 and an exponential. Adaptive Simpson integrates exponential and Lorentzian peaks, against analytic integrals and independent QUADPACK. Quadrature: narrow peaks, cancellation, endpoints and estimator blind spots: Vary Gauss order and adaptive tolerance on narrow Lorentz peaks, a square-root endpoint, severe cancellation, a zero integral and a deliberately missed compact bump, using analytic integrals and QUADPACK.

items.label: Markov-chain Monte Carlo / MCMC
items.scope: Gaussian-target MCMC: distribution, autocorrelation and ESS: Check 32 Metropolis chains against a known standard-normal target; record mean, variance, CDF, autocorrelation time, ESS and sample-budget dependence. Multimodal MCMC: trapping, false reassurance and a global proposal: Compare dispersed local MH, same-mode local MH and symmetry-informed reflection/local MH on the same bimodal target. Separate detecting expected mixing failures from successful finite-budget mode exploration. Independent MCMC diagnostic checks: rank Rhat, bulk/tail ESS and degeneracies: Actually process62 byte-identical datasets with separately installed ArviZ0.20.0, bound by recipe/input/chain/official-source hashes. Separate finite-value agreement from explicit degeneracy-policy differences.

items.label: Radiation transport and moment methods
items.scope: Discrete-ordinate radiation transport through an absorbing slab: Discretize steady pure-absorption transfer in angle and space, checking Beer–Lambert rays and integrated exit flux. Radiation transport: space/angle convergence and photon statistics: Compare characteristics, independent adaptive integration and photon survival in a pure-absorption slab; separate discrete balance, sampling error and interval coverage.

items.label: DSMC and kinetic transport
items.scope: Conservation and Maxwell relaxation in a homogeneous DSMC collision component: Test conservation and relaxation toward equilibrium through randomized pair collisions of homogeneous Maxwell molecules. DSMC collision component: finite-N equilibrium, invariants and statistical error: Distinguish finite-particle equilibrium from the Maxwell limit; compare independent sphere samples, analytic anisotropy decay and across-seed uncertainty.

items.label: Langevin thermostat
items.scope: Langevin thermostat: canonical distributions, timestep bias and correlation: Compare harmonic BAOAB with canonical and discrete-Lyapunov stationary distributions, and with continuous/discrete time correlations. CSVR versus Langevin: distributions, fluctuations and correlations of two harmonic modes: Compare global CSVR with local Langevin on two nondegenerate modes using the same OBABO splitting. Record position, momentum, temperature and total-energy distributions, fluctuations and correlations. Anharmonic CSVR versus Langevin: distribution checks against Boltzmann quadrature: Compare CSVR and Langevin distributions, temperature/energy fluctuations and correlations for two weakly quartic modes. Independent Boltzmann quadrature provides equilibrium references.

items.label: Stochastic velocity rescaling (CSVR)
items.scope: Exact CSVR bath: conditional laws, fluctuations and kinetic correlation: Implement the bath-only CSVR update for 1, 2 and 6 degrees of freedom; compare exact conditional moments/noncentral-chi-square laws, canonical Gamma fluctuations and kinetic correlations. CSVR versus Langevin: distributions, fluctuations and correlations of two harmonic modes: Compare global CSVR with local Langevin on two nondegenerate modes using the same OBABO splitting. Record position, momentum, temperature and total-energy distributions, fluctuations and correlations. Anharmonic CSVR versus Langevin: distribution checks against Boltzmann quadrature: Compare CSVR and Langevin distributions, temperature/energy fluctuations and correlations for two weakly quartic modes. Independent Boltzmann quadrature provides equilibrium references.

items.label: Lie–Trotter splitting
items.scope: Advance a 32-point Schnakenberg reaction–diffusion problem to T=1 with matched inputs and subsolvers. Four step sizes check first-/second-order temporal convergence, reference sensitivity, reaction balance and failure on nonconvergence in a lightweight comparison.

items.label: Strang splitting
items.scope: Advance a 32-point Schnakenberg reaction–diffusion problem to T=1 with matched inputs and subsolvers. Four step sizes check first-/second-order temporal convergence, reference sensitivity, reaction balance and failure on nonconvergence in a lightweight comparison.

items.label: Level-set method
items.scope: Prescribed circle translation and off-center full rotation only: 2D ENO2/Heun,32²/64²/128²,T1, optional redistancing, five common observations and anN64 CFL-halving sensitivity.

items.label: Volume-of-fluid / VOF
items.scope: VOF/CLSVOF comparisons describe formulations and conditions. No VOF implementation, performance ranking, curvature-flow, two-phase-flow or topology-change validation is claimed.
